reviewType: AI-assisted primary-source factual review; not clinical approval

entries.name: ABBV-295
entries.summary: AbbVie reported detailed multiple-ascending-dose Phase 1 findings on 30 September 2026 for subcutaneous ABBV-295, an investigational long-acting amylin analogue. Sixty participants in the reported cohorts received weekly, every-other-week or monthly regimens for 12 or 13 weeks; advancement into Phase 2 was stated as a plan, not a completed start.
entries.ukAuthorisation: The reviewed evidence does not establish UK marketing authorisation for this programme or any dosing regimen.
entries.nhsEngland: No NICE recommendation or NHS England access is established by the reviewed evidence.
entries.supply: Early clinical development does not establish lawful UK retail supply, pharmacy stock or a product sold by Shift Some Timber.
entries.limitations: Small, early sponsor-reported cohorts with 88% male participants. Weight, tolerability and pharmacokinetic observations do not establish long-term efficacy or safety, superiority, a Phase 2 start or future extended-dose regimens. AbbVie states that no regulator has approved ABBV-295.

entries.name: ASC30 oral tablet
entries.summary: The sponsor-submitted registry records a completed 125-participant US Phase 2 study of once-daily oral ASC30 in adults with obesity or overweight. Ascletis later presented sponsor-reported 13-week results; the registry itself still has no posted results.
entries.ukAuthorisation: The reviewed evidence does not establish UK marketing authorisation for oral ASC30.
entries.nhsEngland: No NICE recommendation or NHS England access is established by the reviewed evidence.
entries.supply: A completed US trial and sponsor presentation do not establish lawful UK retail supply, pharmacy stock or a product sold by Shift Some Timber.
entries.limitations: Sponsor-reported Phase 2 findings are not a UK regulatory decision or long-term evidence. The oral formulation is kept separate from the depot injection, and registry completion is not treated as approval or supply.

additionalEvidence.title: Ascletis ADA 2026 programme announcement
additionalEvidence.checkScope: Original sponsor announcement read for the oral Phase 2 presentation and formulation distinction; not automatically content-monitored.

additionalEvidence.title: ClinicalTrials.gov NCT07002905
additionalEvidence.checkScope: Sponsor-submitted registry read for completed Phase 2 status, actual 3 July to 8 December 2025 dates, 125-participant enrolment, daily oral design and absence of posted results; not automatically content-monitored.

entries.name: ASC30 subcutaneous depot
entries.stage: Phase 2 sponsor results; investigational monthly and maintenance regimens
entries.summary: Ascletis reported a 65-participant US Phase 2 study of two subcutaneous depot formulations on 10 March 2026. Formulation A1 was given monthly three times; the sponsor described less-frequent maintenance dosing as a development possibility, not an authorised regimen.
entries.ukAuthorisation: The reviewed evidence does not establish UK marketing authorisation for either ASC30 depot formulation or dosing schedule.
entries.nhsEngland: No NICE recommendation or NHS England access is established by the reviewed evidence.
entries.supply: Sponsor-reported Phase 2 findings do not establish lawful UK retail supply, pharmacy stock or a product sold by Shift Some Timber.
entries.limitations: Sponsor topline results from a small early study. Monthly treatment and quarterly maintenance are development interpretations, not approved regimens. Formulation A2 did not achieve therapeutic exposure in the reported study and is not represented as equivalent to A1 or to oral ASC30.

additionalEvidence.title: Ascletis ASC30 depot Phase 2 announcement
additionalEvidence.checkScope: Original sponsor announcement read for participant count, formulation-specific exposure, dosing, sponsor-reported results and planned maintenance interpretation; not automatically content-monitored.

additionalEvidence.title: ClinicalTrials.gov NCT06679959
additionalEvidence.checkScope: Sponsor-linked registry record retained for the depot study identifier; exact registry publication and update dates were not independently verified in this run, so they remain unknown; not automatically content-monitored.

entries.name: TERN-601
entries.stage: Phase 2 completed; sponsor decided not to advance the programme
entries.summary: Terns reported 12-week Phase 2 FALCON findings in October 2025. Its subsequent quarterly filing states that the company would not advance TERN-601 or invest in other metabolic assets, so it is retained as a stopped programme rather than an advancing oral GLP-1 candidate.
entries.ukAuthorisation: The reviewed evidence does not establish UK marketing authorisation for TERN-601.
entries.nhsEngland: No NICE recommendation or NHS England access is established by the reviewed evidence.
entries.supply: A completed trial does not establish lawful UK retail supply, pharmacy stock or a product sold by Shift Some Timber.
entries.limitations: The sponsor's portfolio decision is recorded separately from the Phase 2 trial observations. Completed research is not approval, and stopping internal development does not prove that every future licensing or research possibility is impossible.

entries.name: Bimagrumab with tirzepatide
entries.stage: Phase 2 active, not recruiting; study completion estimated January 2027
entries.summary: Lilly's sponsor page and registry record an active, not recruiting Phase 2 study of bimagrumab, tirzepatide and their combination in 252 adults with obesity or overweight without diabetes. Primary completion was 16 January 2026, while overall study completion remains estimated for January 2027.
entries.ukAuthorisation: The reviewed evidence does not establish UK marketing authorisation for bimagrumab alone or with tirzepatide for weight management.
entries.nhsEngland: No NICE recommendation or NHS England access is established by the reviewed evidence.
entries.supply: Trial activity does not establish lawful UK retail supply, pharmacy stock or a product sold by Shift Some Timber.
entries.limitations: Active-not-recruiting status and completed enrolment are not results. Body-composition or lean-mass aims do not establish improved strength, function, long-term outcomes or clinical benefit. The trial must remain distinct from BELIEVE with semaglutide and from a separate discontinued type 2 diabetes study.
